To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C-terminal PD2-binding motif in Kv1.5 channels is required for the stimulatory effect of NHERF proteins and SGK1, that NHERF2 is a novel activator of Kv1.5 and that SGK1 and the second PDZ-domain of NHERF are required for maximal stimulation of Kv1.3 and Kv1.5 by NHERF proteins.
NHERFs regulate Kv1.5 channel surface abundance and clustering of signal transduction proteins.

the NHERFs NHERF1/2 modulate Kv1.5 function and cell surface expression by interaction with its C-terminal PDZ binding motif, and that SGK1 and the second PDZ-binding domain of NHERFs are involved in the regulation of Kv1.5 by NHERFs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NHERF1, NHERF2, and SGK1 on the regulation of voltage-gated Kv1.5 potassium channels.
the role of NHERF proteins in the regulation of Kv1.5 channel activity and abundance in the heart and in the brain.
the regulation of the Kv1.3 potassium channel by the Na+/K+-ATPase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NHERFs are involved in the regulation of Kv1.5 and other Kv channels, and that they are important in the modulation of the cardiac action potential.
the C-terminal PD domain on Kv1. 5 is responsible for the interaction of Kv1.5 and NHERF1/2 and that the interaction of these two proteins is responsible for the modulation of Kv1. 3.
NHERFs participate in the regulation and clustering of Kv1.5 and other ion channels by controlling their surface abundance and by recruiting signaling molecules to the channel complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NHERF2 and SGK1 synergize to activate Kv1.
the C-terminal PDZip motif in Kv1.5 channels is a crucial determinant for NHERF2-mediated regulation of the Kv1.
NHERF2 and SGK1 cooperate in the modulation of Kv1.5 by interacting with the channel via the C-terminal PDZD-binding motif and the second PDZ-domain in NHERF-2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N- and C-termini of the Kv1.3 and Kv1.5 channels contain PDZ-binding motifs that might be recognized and modulated by PDZ domain-containing scaffold proteins such as NHERF1/2.
the C-terminal PD2 domain in the Kv1 family of potassium channels is important for the modulation of the channels by the NHERF proteins.
Kv1.5 and NHERF are involved in the regulation of the cardiac action potential.
